title: Projection normalized reindexing of quotient completion and completed tensor
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$, $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ for a scheme $W$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Let $g:X\xrightarrow{\sim}Y$ be a scheme isomorphism, with $\ell$ invertible on both schemes [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Put $F=g^{-1}$, with the coefficient identifications induced by all quotient projections. Use the coefficient-stage derived operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom].

Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ with the strict quotient transitions, $F_\bullet$ for reindexing strict coefficient systems, and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$, the total derived limit computed by a K-injective resolution of the strict tower [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus, lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. There are canonical natural identifications
$$F_\bullet\mathcal R_YK\cong\mathcal R_XFK,\qquad F\mathcal L_YA\cong\mathcal L_XF_\bullet A.$$
They respect every quotient arrow and limit projection and the actual reduction/limit adjunction unit and counit. For derived-complete $K$ the canonical unit $u_K:K\to\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YK$ is an isomorphism, and the specified comparison
$$FK\xrightarrow{F(u_K)}F\mathcal L_Y\mathcal R_YK\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal L_XF_\bullet\mathcal R_YK=Lg^*K$$
is a natural isomorphism with all reduction projections fixed. Here completeness and the quotient-unit normalization are those of [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison] for $L=E$, not just existence of a limit triangle.

For derived-complete constructible $M,N$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], the ordinary reindexing of the strict tensor-reduction complexes gives an isomorphism
$$F(M\widehat\otimes^L N)\xrightarrow{\sim}FM\widehat\otimes^L FN.$$
Under the preceding pullback identification it equals precisely the canonical comparison of [def-pur-completed-pullback-tensor-comparison]. On a flat-term K-flat representative it reindexes each total-tensor summand; on the fixed Roos realization it reindexes both product coordinates and $1-s$, including the cone shift. Its inverse is reverse reindexing. Coefficient transitions, symmetry, associators, identity and composition of scheme isomorphisms, and signed shifts commute with these identifications on the actual systems and their functorial realizations, with the substitution normalization of [lem-pur-completed-operation-tower-substitution].

proof.text: For the ambient declaration combine strict reindexing with its derived localization. Obtain quotient generator and transition formulas from isomorphismReductionTower. Compare primitive completion with the selected adjunction using uniqueness of left adjoints. Derive counit compatibility from unit compatibility and the triangle identities. Normalized reconstruction inverts the actual unit on complete inputs, and the limit and pullback isomorphisms invert the specified ordinary-to-completed map.

For each isomorphism choose its normalized completion comparison from the proved ambient assertion. Apply the strict tensor construction to the same datum to obtain its normalized tensor comparison. Assemble these assignments using the family-coherence theorem, which adds only the section-normalized identity and composition isomorphisms and proves all family tensor constraints. These are local choices inside an existence proof; no definition is populated from mere existence.

For every complete input apply podOrdinaryToCompleted_isIso to the complete unit provided by normalized reconstruction. For a constructible input K choose a prime p>l+1, form the finite-field datum over ZMod p, and apply sfDerivedComplete_iff_legacy to K.property.1. This yields IntegralOnSlice.IsComplete, so the same ambient argument proves the constructible-input isomorphism.

Apply the signed-shift construction to the selected completion and tensor data at g. For each coefficient embedding E→L, construct Dprime with the proved ambient completion theorem at L and extend it to Tprime using the tensor construction theorem. Apply the scalar-transition theorem to these fixed E and L data. Apply normalized substitution to the same original E data. Combine these witnesses with family coherence and the ambient isomorphism assertions. Each imported theorem is strictly one part of the argument, and the final Lean proof combines them without a hole.
